Rule made returnable forthwith.
The writ petition is heard finally with consent of the learned counsel for the parties.

By this petition, the petitioner, a Partnership firm is seeking declaration that the reservation of land admeasuring 1 Hectare 39 Are WP 4535-19 2 Judgment from Survey No.5/2 and 50 Are from Survey No.7/1 at Mouza- Wanjri, P.H. 1 No.10(422), House No.2305, Ward No.57, situated near Pili Nadi, Wanjri, Kamptee road, Nagpur belonging to the petitioner has lapsed and the land is free for the purpose of development as is otherwise permissible in the case of adjacent land under the relevant plan.
Further, the petitioner seeks a direction to the respondent no.1 to notify the lapsing of reservation of the aforesaid lands by notifying the same by an order published in the official gazette.
3. The aforesaid lands have been included in "Green Belt Control Scheme".

They are earmarked in the final development plan as having reserved for three different purposes viz. MN58 for Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation (ST Stand); MN107 for Nagpur Improvement Trust Office; and MN108 for Nagpur Municipal Corporation Zonal Office.
The final development plan came into force on March 01, 2000.

Since no steps were taken by the Planning Authority to acquire the lands for the purpose for which they were reserved for a period of more than 10 years from the date on which final development plan came into force, the petitioner served a notice upon respondents under Section 127 of the Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act, 1966 (for short, 'the Act of 1966') dated October 01, 2016.

entities.text: Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act, 1966
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: WP 4535-19 3 Judgment 4.

Shri Aditya Chaudhari, learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the reservation of lands of the petitioner for Nagpur Municipal Corporation Zonal Office, Nagpur Improvement Trust Office and Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation has lapsed since the respondents did not take effective steps for the acquisition of the same within a period of 24 months from the date of service of the notice.
It is submitted that the purchase notice was served upon the respondents on October 01, 2016 alongwith the documents showing title.
It was incumbent upon the respondents to take effective steps for the acquisition before September 30, 2018.

It is claimed that since steps for the acquisition of lands were not taken, it would be necessary to grant a declaration that the reservation of lands of the petitioner has lapsed in view of section 127 of the Act of 1966.

He would further submit that as per section 127(2) of the Act of 1966 on lapsing of reservation, allocation or designation of any land under Section 127(1) of the Act of 1966, the Government shall notify the same, by an order published in the official gazette.

He would also urge to consider the communication dated November 13, 2006 whereby Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation for whom part of land was reserved has expressed its clear disinterest in the aforesaid lands.

The counsel for the petitioner would further submit that the Planning Authority cannot force upon the land owner to exercise an option of obtaining TDR as WP 4535-19 4 Judgment per their own convenience and it cannot be sustained in the eyes of law.

In support of the aforesaid contentions,
the counsel for the petitioner has relied upon the judgments in Chhabildas Versus State of Maharashtra & Others [(2018) 2 SCC 784] and Mohandas and Others v/s. State of Maharashtra and others [2020 SCC OnLine SC 97].

2 communication dated July 13, 2017 whereby the petitioner was asked to supply the necessary documents which consist of demarcated measurement sheet from the City Survey Department so that appropriate process of identifying the area of reservation could be undertaken.
It is submitted that in view of such non-compliance, the petition lacks merit.

Further, by letter dated March 14,
2016 the said respondents have offered Transferable Development Rights (TDR) to the petitioner for which appropriate application was asked to be made.
However, the petitioner has not made any application till date.
Hence, it cannot be WP 4535-19 5 Judgment said that no effective steps were taken for acquisition by the said respondent within 24 months as per section 127 of the Act of 1966.

6. Shri. S.M. Puranik, learned counsel for respondents no. 2 and 3 at the outset strongly opposed the prayer made in the petition and would submit that by the communication dated July 13, 2017 the petitioner was offered TDR which was denied by the petitioner.
Therefore, it cannot be said that no effective steps are taken by the said respondents for the acquisition within 24 months as per section 127 of the Act of 1966.
7. We have appreciated the aforesaid submissions.

8. On a plain reading of Section 127(1) of the Act of 1966, it is clear that the petitioner has satisfied the condition of serving of a notice alongwith the documents showing his title or interest on the respondents as the lands were not acquired by agreement within ten years from the date on which final development plan came into force.
The respondent ought to have acquired the land or taken steps towards acquisition within 24 months i.e. before September 30, 2018.
9. The petitioner has rightly relied on the recent judgments of the Apex Court in the cases of Chhabildas and Mohandas (supra).
In the former judgment, the Apex Court at Length discussed 'steps towards WP 4535-19 6 Judgment the acquisition' and the same view has been reiterated in the latter judgment.

It is well settled that the steps towards acquisition commences when active steps are taken for the acquisition of land which leads to publication of declaration under Section 6 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 read with the provisions of Section 126 of the Act of 1966.
The same has been held in various judgments of the Courts.

10. Further, it is also no more res integra that merely offering TDR would not be in compliance of Section 127 of the Act of 1966 and it is not obligatory on the petitioner to accept the TDR in lieu of the compensation.

The full bench judgment of this Court in Shree Vinayak Builders and Developers,
Nagpur (supra) relied on by the petitioner

entities.text:
Shree Vinayak Builders and Developers,
Nagpur
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: has held that mere grant of approval or passing of resolution by the Authorities concerned for grant of TDR/FSI in lieu of monetary compensation is not a step towards the acquisition of land and the land owner cannot be compelled to accept the same.
The Full Bench has also considered the issue of what constitutes a step commencing the acquisition proceeding elaborately.

11. The petitioner has also drawn our attention to the judgment rendered by the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in M/s Jaika Vanijya Ltd. & Another (supra), wherein the Court has granted the requisite relief for adjoining land affected by the similar reservation.

As a consequence of above discussion, we deem it appropriate to allow the present writ petition.

It is hereby declared that the reservation of the lands of the petitioner admeasuring 1 Hectare 39 Are from Survey No.5/2 and 50 Are from Survey No.7/1 at Mouza- Wanjri, P.H. No.17/A, bearing City Survey Nos.14 and 15, Sheet No.10 (422), House No.2305, Ward No.57, situated near Pili Nadi,
Wanjri, Kamptee road, Nagpur has lapsed and the lands are free for the purpose of development as is otherwise permissible to the adjacent land under the development plan.

The respondent no. 1 is directed to notify lapsing of the reservation on the aforesaid lands by notifying the same by an order published in the official gazette as per section 127(2) of the Act of 1966 within eight weeks from the date of producing the copy of this judgment.
13. Rule is made absolute in aforesaid terms.
No costs.
